v.why: Filling the empty direct input-output edge with a conv adds a strong residual path, while replacing an existing skip/pool brings little or negative gain (exp 1-2 vs 4-7).
Replacing the identity shortcut on edge 3 with a conv loses the residual path and hurts accuracy (exp 4-5, inverse of 25).
Adding a shortcut where none existed gives large gains (exp 26) compared with replacing conv/pool ops on edge 3 (exp 25, 27, 28).
With edge 5 absent, edge 3 carries more of the output signal, so upgrading it matters more (exp 2 vs 1, 7 vs 6).
Removing edge 5 when edge 3 is absent leaves few or no paths to the output, which can collapse accuracy (exp 14, 18 vs 13, 17).
Without the direct edge 3, removing edge 0 can disconnect the cell (exp 23, 24 vs 19-22).
Skip-dominated cells are very weak, so swapping a skip for a conv yields large gains (exp 53, 91) compared with replacing a 1x1 conv (exp 65).
Removing a parameter-free skip on edge 0 costs nothing or even helps (exp 76), whereas removing a conv loses capacity (exp 19-24).
Adding any learnable op on the empty direct edge gives big gains (exp 98), while replacing a 3x3 conv with 1x1 is roughly neutral (exp 69).
Adding a shortcut into the output where none existed helps more than replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 5 (exp 30 vs 29).

raw:
Ten hypotheses, each grounded in the measured edits:

- **Edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3:**
  - Gains are larger when edge 3 was `none` (experiments 1, 2: +2.2 to +12 points) than when it was skip or avg_pool (experiments 4–7: roughly zero or negative).
  - Gains are smaller when it replaces a skip connection.
  - Gains are larger when edge 5 is `none` (experiment 2 vs 1, experiment 7 vs 6).
- **Edge 3 → skip_connect or nor_conv_1x1:** both gain most when they fill an empty edge 3 (experiments 26, 98). The direct input-to-output path matters a lot, especially on ImageNet16-120.
- **Removing an edge (→ none):** this hurts more when edge 3 is already `none`, because the cell can become disconnected (experiments 18, 23, 24).
- **Replacing a skip connection with a 3x3 conv:** gains are higher, since skip-heavy cells do poorly (experiments 49–53).
- **Removing edge 0:** this hurts less, and can even help, when edge 0 was a skip connection (experiment 76).
- **Edge 5 → skip_connect:** this helps more when it fills an empty edge 5 (experiment 30 vs 29).
